sources.name: I LOVE NY (New York State tourism)
New York State Parks & Historic Sites

sights.w: 500-acre open-air sculpture park in the Hudson Highlands with monumental works by Calder, Serra, di Suvero, and a Maya Lin earthwork set across meadows and hills.
sights.k: Hudson Valley (Orange County); ~1.5 hr drive, or Metro-North to Beacon plus shuttle. Seasonal (spring-fall), closed Tuesdays.

sights.w: Dia's collection of 1960s-to-present minimal and land art in a former Nabisco box-printing factory, with vast daylit galleries of Richard Serra, Agnes Martin, and Dan Flavin.
sights.k: Hudson Valley (Dutchess County); ~80 min on the Metro-North Hudson line to Beacon. Open Fri-Mon.

sights.n: Walkway Over the Hudson State Historic Park
sights.w: The world's longest elevated pedestrian bridge, a 1.28-mile former railroad span 212 feet above the Hudson linking Poughkeepsie and Highland.
sights.k: Hudson Valley (Dutchess County); ~1.75 hr drive, or Metro-North to Poughkeepsie. Free; open daily 7am-sunset.

sights.w: Six-story Rockefeller family mansion above the Hudson with Beaux-Arts gardens, a modern-sculpture collection, and a coach barn of classic cars and carriages.
sights.k: Westchester (Sleepy Hollow); ~45 min drive. Guided tours only from the Philipsburg Manor visitor center. Tours are SUSPENDED for the 2026 season; confirm before visiting.

sights.address: 3006 Seven Lakes Drive, Bear Mountain, NY 10911
sights.w: Hudson Highlands park with a summit auto road and Perkins Tower views toward the Manhattan skyline, a lakeside 1920s inn, a trailside zoo, and a merry-go-round.
sights.k: Hudson Valley (Rockland/Orange counties); ~1 hr drive. Open year-round.

sights.w: Well-preserved 19th-century riverfront village of antique shops and cafes across from Storm King, a gateway to Breakneck Ridge and Hudson Highlands hiking.
sights.k: Hudson Valley (Putnam County); ~80 min on the Metro-North Hudson line, walkable straight from the station.

sights.address: 2107 New South Post Road, West Point, NY 10996
sights.w: The nation's oldest continuously operating Army post and academy above the Hudson; public bus tours visit Trophy Point, the Cadet Chapel, and Battle Monument.
sights.k: Hudson Valley (Orange County); ~1.5 hr drive. Access to the post is by guided bus tour only; bring government ID for the required background check.

sights.w: Restored 18th-century Dutch-colonial milling and trading site with a working water mill, telling the story of the 23 enslaved Africans who ran it.
sights.k: Westchester (Sleepy Hollow); ~45 min drive. Timed tours May-early November, Wed-Sun.

sights.address: 200 Morris Pesin Drive, Jersey City, NJ 07305
sights.w: Waterfront NJ park facing the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island, with the restored 1889 Central Railroad terminal, a 2-mile promenade, and ferries to the monuments.
sights.k: New Jersey (Jersey City); ~25 min via PATH plus a short walk, or a quick drive. Open daily 6am-10pm.

sights.w: 42-acre sculpture park and museum on former state fairgrounds, dotted with Seward Johnson's life-size bronzes set among gardens, ponds, and roaming peacocks.
sights.k: New Jersey (Mercer County); ~1.5 hr drive, or NJ Transit to Hamilton. Closed Tuesdays.

sights.w: Ivy League campus of Collegiate Gothic quadrangles anchored by 1756 Nassau Hall, once the U.S. capitol, with a free open-air Putnam sculpture collection.
sights.k: New Jersey (Mercer County); ~1.5 hr by NJ Transit to Princeton Junction plus the Dinky shuttle. Free student-led campus tours.

sights.w: Herzog & de Meuron-designed museum of American art in the Hamptons, strong in East End painters like Fairfield Porter and the region's postwar artists.
sights.k: Long Island (Hamptons/Water Mill); ~2.5 hr drive, or LIRR to Southampton. Closed Tue-Wed.

sights.address: 71 Old Westbury Road, Old Westbury, NY 11568
sights.w: Gold Coast estate of the Phipps family with a 1906 Charles II-style mansion and 200 acres of formal English gardens, ponds, and tree-lined allees.
sights.k: Long Island (Nassau Gold Coast); ~45 min drive. Closed Tuesdays; grounds are seasonal, roughly April-December.

sights.w: Robert Moses's 1929 Atlantic beach with 6.5 miles of sand, an Art Deco bathhouse and water tower, a long boardwalk, and a summer amphitheater.
sights.k: Long Island (Nassau County); ~1 hr drive, or LIRR to Freeport/Wantagh plus a beach-bus shuttle. Busiest on summer weekends.

sights.w: 168-foot black-and-white striped 1858 lighthouse on the barrier-island seashore, with a keepers' museum and a tower climb over the dunes and ocean.
sights.k: Long Island (Fire Island); ~1.5 hr drive via the Robert Moses Causeway to Field 5, then a half-mile boardwalk. Seasonal; tower climbs weather-permitting.

sights.w: New York's oldest lighthouse, authorized under George Washington and lit in 1796, at the easternmost tip of Long Island, with a museum and a tower climb.
sights.k: Long Island (East End); ~3 hr drive or LIRR Montauk line, the farthest of these trips. Seasonal, roughly spring-fall.

sights.w: Long Island wine-country estate near the Hamptons known for its dry rose and sparkling wines, with a year-round tasting room among the vines.
sights.k: Long Island (East End/Sagaponack); ~2.5 hr drive, or LIRR to Bridgehampton plus a short ride. Tasting room open daily; reservations advised.

food.w: Two-Michelin-star farm-to-table destination at the Stone Barns agriculture center, serving a long tasting menu built from the surrounding fields and livestock.
food.k: Westchester (Pocantico Hills); ~45 min drive. Reservation-only, prix fixe; among the country's hardest tables to book.

food.w: Waterfront lobster deck and seafood market on Fort Pond Bay, an order-at-the-counter Montauk institution famed for its lobster roll and sunset harbor views.
food.k: Long Island (Montauk); ~3 hr drive or LIRR Montauk line. Seasonal; casual outdoor picnic-table seating over the water.
